reviewed_sources.title: Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, second edition
reviewed_sources.version: Author-hosted AMS GSM 157, April 2014 preface; 370 PDF pages
reviewed_sources.read_scope: Printed pages 157-159 (PDF pages 169-171): relative boundedness definitions, Lemmas 6.2-6.3 with proofs, Theorem 6.4 with proof, Lemma 6.5 with proof.
reviewed_sources.use: Established common-domain self-adjointness under bounded Hermitian perturbations and second resolvent identity. The note also gives the bounded-perturbation surjectivity argument and the Duhamel/insertion bounds explicitly.
reviewed_sources.limits: The entire book and its upstream spectral-theorem and surjectivity dependencies were not re-reviewed; Duhamel is derived in the note, not attributed to an unread theorem here.

reviewed_sources.title: Bifurcation analysis for axisymmetric capillary water waves with vorticity and swirl
reviewed_sources.version: arXiv:2202.01754v2, submitted 8 March 2022; manuscript dated March 9; 30 PDF pages
reviewed_sources.read_scope: Introduction and governing stream operator on PDF pages 1-3 through browser text; Sections 3.1-3.4 on PDF pages 4-6 through cached text, including the r^2 substitution, axis regularity discussion and lifted five-dimensional equation.
reviewed_sources.use: Established removal of the stream-function axis singularity by the five-dimensional lift. Both transformed differential identities and the geometry-specific boundary barrier are independently derived and symbolically checked.
reviewed_sources.limits: Fluid bifurcation theorems are not used or proof-reviewed. The cited Ni origin and the upstream Cartesian regularity reference were not newly audited. Our argument uses smooth azimuthal fields and the directly checked harmonic lift.

development_notes: The first verifier launch stopped before calculation because embedded Python did not put the sibling checks directory on sys.path. It was replaced by an explicit file-based import. No tolerance or analytic bound was changed for this environment issue.
novelty_decision: Continue the physical long-return question and matched finite-duration fallback. The source-free Maxwell potential is a bounded small Dirac perturbation under an explicit optical comparison condition. The simple cap would exclude the physical RN neck, so an attenuation supersolution replaces it there. Harmonic lifting, bounded perturbation and Duhamel are established; no new physical damping, stability, shortcut or support theorem is accepted.
optical_geometry_review: Independent differentiation of the extremal RN optical radius verifies y*y_double_prime <= 1/2; the standard AdS throat gives a nonpositive product. The RN l=1 test-Maxwell radial identity is checked directly, not imported from the unread 1980 coupled-perturbation paper. The joined physical metric and its global comparison condition remain to be derived.
